transcript.text: Hello, everyone, and thank you for coming to hear about our new community garden. I'm Ms Patel, and I'm the project leader. I'd like to explain what we are planning and how you can help.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: The garden will be on the empty land behind the library, which was a car park until two years ago. The council has agreed that we can use it for ten years, and we will begin work on the first of April.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: I know that some people were sad when the car park closed, but I think that everyone will agree that a garden is a much better use of the space.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: At the moment the ground is covered with concrete in some places, and we need to remove it first. A local company will do this for free, which is a great help, because it would cost a lot.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: After that, we will build raised beds, which are like large wooden boxes filled with soil. They are easier to work in, especially for older people, because you don't need to bend down so much.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: We plan to grow vegetables such as tomatoes, carrots and beans, and also some flowers, because they bring bees and butterflies to the garden. The school next door will have its own small area for the children.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: We have already raised some money. A shop in the high street gave us five hundred pounds, and the tools were donated by a hardware store. We still need to buy compost and seeds, so we are asking for small donations.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: Water is also important. We will collect rain from the roof of the library in large tanks, and that will give us enough water for most of the summer. We don't want to use too much from the pipes.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: What can volunteers do? Well, first we need people for digging and planting, usually on Saturday mornings from ten until twelve. You don't need any experience, and we will show you what to do.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: We also need someone to organise the social events, such as the summer picnic and the harvest party in autumn. If you like meeting people and planning things, this job is perfect for you.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: Another task is to take photographs and write posts on social media. That helps us to find new volunteers and shows the council that the project is popular.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: Everything we grow will be shared. Half will go to the volunteers and the other half to the local food bank, which gives free food to families who have difficulty paying for it.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: Before we start, you will need to wear sensible clothes, and bring gloves if you have them. We will provide the tea and biscuits. If you want to join, please write your name on the list at the back.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL

transcript.text: Thank you very much for listening. I'm sure that this garden will be a special place for our neighbourhood.
transcript.speaker: MS PATEL
